title: Learning from Human Corrections through Temporal Preferences
abstract: arXiv:2611.31446v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: When people intervene to correct a robot, they provide information not only through how they correct its behavior, but also through when they choose to intervene. Existing approaches to Learning from Corrections focus on comparing the new trajectory to the robot's originally intended behavior, thus underutilizing the context of the robot's behavior before the intervention. In this work, we investigate how both pre- and post-intervention behavior can be translated into preference pairs for learning value functions that approximate a human's latent reward. We construct post-intervention preferences by comparing corrected behavior with the behavior it replaces, and pre-intervention preferences from temporal relationships among states leading up to an intervention. translated_title: 通过时间偏好从人类纠正中学习
translated_abstract: 当人们介入纠正机器人时，他们不仅通过纠正机器人行为的方式提供信息，还通过选择何时介入来提供信息。现有的从纠正中学习方法侧重于将新轨迹与机器人原本预期的行为进行比较，因而未能充分利用介入前机器人行为所处的情境。在这项工作中，我们研究了如何将介入前和介入后的行为转化为偏好对，以学习逼近人类潜在奖励的价值函数。我们通过比较纠正后的行为与其所替代的行为来构建介入后偏好，并从导致介入发生的各个状态之间的时间关系中构建介入前偏好。我们通过两个下游任务来评估学习到的价值表示：目标推断和纠正预测。我们的结果表明，介入后偏好是……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出将人类纠正机器人时介入前后的行为及其时间关系转化为偏好对，从而学习更准确逼近人类潜在奖励的价值函数，并在目标推断与纠正预测两个下游任务上验证了其有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes translating both pre- and post-intervention human correction behavior into preference pairs based on temporal relationships, enabling the learning of value functions that better approximate a human's latent reward, validated through goal inference and correction forecasting tasks.
